documents.title: Quick update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, no question really, just wanted to say I've been going for a walk after dinner most nights and started logging my food in an app. Hard to keep it up in this cold but I'm trying! Do I need to come in before summer?

documents.title: RE: Quick update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great to hear, Donna. Keep it going. No need to come in before then unless something changes; we'll do your follow-up and repeat blood work around June.

documents.title: Reschedule
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt has a work deadline Monday and can't make her 6/8 follow-up. Moved to Mon 6/29, 8:15, fasting for labs.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

orders.order: Registered dietitian referral, medical nutrition therapy

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u prediabetes / metabolic syndrome, about a year since we first met.

Last June she was worried about her weight and her desk-bound days and said she was ready to make changes. She has: walking 30 min every evening, signed up for a fitness class at the community center a few weeks ago, mostly off sweetened drinks, and counting calories in a phone app. Feels better day to day. No new symptoms. Still no medications.

She asks whether a nutritionist would help her keep going. I think it would - she has done the hard part of building habits and a dietitian can fine-tune the eating side. She clearly understands the plan and where she wants to take it; her call and a good one.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Comfortable. Heart RRR, lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
- Prediabetes, metabolic syndrome, obesity, dyslipidemia (high TG / low HDL): continue lifestyle program. Fasting A1c, glucose, lipids and CMP drawn today. Referral to registered dietitian for medical nutrition therapy placed.
- No meds.
- Annual physical already on the books for late July.

documents.title: June labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Donna - results from Monday are back. A1c, fasting sugar, triglycerides and HDL are all close to where they were last year: still the prediabetes picture, not worse. Liver and kidney numbers normal. It often takes a while for blood work to catch up with new habits, so keep at it. We can go over them in detail at your physical on the 28th.

documents.title: Dietitian referral
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Nutrition office called - referral and last office note received, insurance verified for MNT. They will contact pt directly to book; first openings are in September.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 45F.

Interval: seen 6/29 for metabolic follow-up; dietitian referral in process, nutrition office expects September. Keeping up the evening walks and the class twice a week. No complaints. Sleeping OK. Mood good.
Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker, weekend wine only.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. NAD. Eyes, ears, oropharynx normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement, no nodes. Heart regular rate, no murmurs. Lungs clear throughout. Breast exam declined, mammogram scheduled. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities without edema. Skin no suspicious lesions. Neuro grossly intact.

Reviewed June labs with her: A1c and fasting glucose in prediabetic range, TG still high, HDL still low, CMP fine.

Plan:
- Prediabetes / metabolic syndrome / obesity / dyslipidemia: lifestyle plan, dietitian. Recheck A1c and lipids at a December visit.
- Screening: mammogram ordered; FIT kit handed to her; cervical screening next due 2028; PHQ-2 0.
- Vaccines: flu and COVID when the fall supply arrives; Tdap good until 2029.
December follow-up booked at checkout.
